summary: Dashboard ConfidenceDot micro-indicator + Confidence·Triage header link fully verified on desktop + mobile (390px). 18 dots render (14 signal + 4 pattern) across admin's 18 alerts, grey by default (no resolved trades yet) with correct 'no trades taken yet' tooltips. Mocked-stats run validated GREEN (72% signal) and AMBER (50% pattern) color+tooltip paths. Zero console errors. Regression clean: mark-all-read, deep-link to /analysis/{ticker}, unread count badge logic all unchanged. Backend skipped per review_request (frontend-only iteration).
critical_code_review_comments: DashboardPage.jsx ConfidenceDot branch comment in the header JSDoc (line 153) says 'AMBER — 45–60% OR <3 resolved' but the actual code routes <3 resolved to the GREY branch (line 172). Comment is stale/misleading — update to reflect real behaviour: AMBER = 45≤wr<60 AND ≥3 resolved.

fetchAlerts() fires /alerts and /alerts/stats in parallel but stats is a detached .then() without error state (silently swallowed .catch(() => {})). If the stats endpoint 500s, dots stay grey forever with no user-facing signal. Consider a console.warn at minimum, consistent with fetchQuota() which does log.

rf_watchlist_scan alerts — admin currently has 0 of this type so the RED-path rendering was only validated by forcing via mocked response. Logic is sound but there is no production coverage today; seed at least one rf_watchlist_scan alert with taken+resolved losses to exercise RED in an e2e run.

ConfidenceDot uses flexShrink:0 inline but relies on the parent flex gap for spacing; on very long ticker symbols in 390px viewport the row still fits (verified), but a min-width on the ticker span would future-proof overflow.
